rationale: Olden/power is a pointer-intensive healthcare simulation built around a person binary tree, driven by a hot multi-year simulation loop with hash-table lookups and recursive tree traversals; the static profile is empty, so the table leans on these known characteristics. Instruction substitution (SUB) and basic-block splitting (SPLIT) are cheap, always-safe transforms with low size growth, so they get high application weights with low cost/risk weights to provide a baseline of static-analysis resistance everywhere. Control-flow flattening (FLA) and bogus control flow (BCF) offer the largest reverse-engineering resistance on the dispatch/simulation loops, but both sit directly on power's hottest execution paths, so their SecurityGain weights are high while elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights let the feature-driven selector withhold them from frequently-executed functions and concentrate them on cold ones (setup, tree construction, I/O). Indirect-branch (IBR), indirect-call (ICALL), and global-variable (IGV) indirection are well matched to this program's call/branch and linked-structure profile and defeat pointer/CFG recovery analysis at modest runtime cost, so they carry strong DiversityGain weights with moderate risk weights, since indirection on the tree-chasing code must be applied selectively to keep the simulation loop's overhead acceptable and preserve correctness across the recursive traversals.
